Traupman 125

trānsenna, trānsennae f.

noun, first declension

roller shutter, blind

Jack’s ruling. Classically a net or a lattice.

Examples

  • trānsennam dēmittere / subdūcere

    let down / pull up the shuttercomposed

  • cum pater, trānsennā dēmissā lūmineque exstīnctō

    when Dad, after letting down the shutter and turning off the lightLibellus II, Sintra: castellum et puteus

  • fenestra ampla, trānsennā jam subductā, arborēs prōspiciēbat

    a big window, its shutter already up, looked out on the treesLibellus III, Apud avum et aviam

See also shutter, window.

SourcesLewis & Short: transenna

John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 125, checked against the searchable text of the book (29 October 2026).
